title: HDFC Bank Q1 Profit Rises 5% to ₹19,060 Crore as Provisions Plunge
excerpt: India's largest private lender posted steady earnings growth in the June quarter, broadly meeting analyst estimates, as a sharp drop in bad-loan provisions offset a decline in treasury income.
body:
• Standalone net profit rose 5% year-on-year to ₹19,060 crore ($1.98 billion), in line with the LSEG consensus estimate of ₹19,190 crore
  • Provisions and contingencies plunged 78% to ₹3,060 crore from ₹14,442 crore a year ago, when the bank built floating and contingent reserves
  • Gross advances grew 15.4% year-on-year driven by retail loans, while net interest margin held at 3.26% — still below the pre-merger 4% level
  • Board appointed former bureaucrat Rajiv Kumar as chairman last month after Atanu Chakraborty's resignation in March

HDFC Bank on Saturday reported a 5% rise in standalone net profit to ₹19,060 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, broadly meeting analyst expectations as a sharp decline in provisions for bad loans compensated for weaker treasury income.

The Mumbai-based lender had earned ₹18,155 crore in the year-ago period. Analysts surveyed by LSEG had forecast earnings of ₹19,190 crore, according to Reuters.

Margins and Revenue

Net interest income — the gap between interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits — rose 7% to ₹33,530 crore from ₹31,440 crore a year earlier, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. The net interest margin held steady at 3.26% on total assets but remained well below the 4% level the bank maintained before its $40 billion merger with parent HDFC Ltd in 2023.

Interest income rose to ₹79,363 crore from ₹77,470 crore. Total income, however, fell to ₹92,184 crore from ₹99,200 crore, dragged down by a 41% quarter-on-quarter drop in other income from treasury operations and fee income to ₹12,821 crore. Rising bond yields and the RBI's curbs on forex options hurt banks' treasury income across the sector.

Operating profit declined to ₹28,169 crore from ₹35,734 crore a year ago, when the bank had booked outsized trading gains.

Asset Quality Holds

The standout line in the results was provisions. At ₹3,060 crore, provisions and contingencies fell 78% from ₹14,442 crore in Q1 FY26 — a quarter in which the bank had set aside ₹9,000 crore in floating provisions and ₹1,700 crore in contingent provisions as part of its countercyclical strategy.

Gross non-performing assets improved to 1.17% of gross advances from 1.40% a year earlier, though they edged up from 1.15% in the March quarter. Net NPAs declined to 0.41% from 0.47% year-on-year. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 19.57%, down marginally from 19.88%.

Loan Growth Accelerates

HDFC Bank's advances grew 15.4% year-on-year at end-June, driven primarily by retail loans including mortgages and personal debt, Reuters reported. Total deposits rose 13.3%.

Indian banks have seen a pickup in loan growth since April, with demand for personal credit and loans against gold rising. Small businesses have also stepped up borrowing, in part backed by government default guarantees made available amid disruptions from the West Asia conflict.

The consolidated profit after tax of the HDFC Bank Group rose 18% to ₹19,245 crore from ₹16,258 crore, with consolidated net revenue at ₹85,480 crore.

Governance and Outlook

The results come as HDFC Bank navigates a period of leadership transition. Part-time chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned in March citing ethical differences. The bank completed a legal review that found no evidence to support the concerns he raised. Former bureaucrat Rajiv Kumar was appointed chairman last month, but the bank is yet to apply for reappointment of CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan.

Analysts have kept a positive stance. Bernstein, which holds an outperform rating with a ₹1,150 target, noted that loan growth of 15.4% was broadly in line with the banking system, while deposit growth of 14.7% ran ahead of industry trends. Morgan Stanley maintained an overweight rating with a ₹1,025 target, citing attractive valuations relative to the stock's historical bands.

HDFC Bank shares closed at ₹819.60 on the NSE on Friday, up 1.4% on the day.
